name: One Faith, Many Churches
description: From a teacher in Roman Judea to monks, reformers, missionaries and popes: how Christianity spread and split into the many traditions of today.

checkpoints.name: The first followers
checkpoints.note: Jesus taught in Galilee and Judea, and after his death his followers spread the message through the Roman world. Paul the apostle carried it to Gentile cities and wrote letters that became part of the Christian scriptures.

checkpoints.name: Empire, monks and friars
checkpoints.note: Constantine ended official persecution and Christianity grew with state support. Augustine shaped Western theology, Benedict gave monks a rule, Francis and the friars preached in towns, and Aquinas joined faith to philosophy. Lalibela in Ethiopia has churches carved from rock.

checkpoints.name: The Western church divides
checkpoints.note: Printing carried the Bible to new readers. Martin Luther sparked the Protestant Reformation, Zwingli and Calvin built reformed churches, Henry VIII created the Church of England, and Ignatius founded the Jesuits as Catholic reform gathered pace.

checkpoints.name: Awakenings and new movements
checkpoints.note: Quakers, the Latter-day Saints founded by Joseph Smith and the Salvation Army arose outside the older state churches, while Methodism, led by John Wesley, began as a revival inside the Church of England before it became a separate church. Many of these movements spread widely beyond Europe.

checkpoints.name: A global faith
checkpoints.note: Christianity became a worldwide religion with large communities on every continent. Figures such as Mother Teresa, Pope John Paul II and Pope Francis became known far beyond their own churches, and the Opus Dei movement grew within Catholicism.
